objective: Preregister and batch-screen the leveraged-ETF close-rebalancing flow reversal mechanism (dir:letf_close_rebalancing_flow_reversal) on SPY/QQQ/SMH: a large one-day down move forces daily leverage-ratio rebalancing that the literature associates with next-day mean reversion in the underlying. For scripts/screen_batch.py --batch h20260929_01_letf_flow_reversal --iteration h20260929_01_letf_flow_reversal. No return, Sharpe or backtest number is computed in this dossier.

sources.core_claim: Survey of the leveraged/inverse-ETF rebalancing-flow literature: 'the literature consistently reports statistically significant associations between ETF rebalancing demand and late-day returns and volatility' but 'most of the available papers suffer from potentially serious methodological errors, and the economic associations appear to be insignificant'; overall 'concerns raised by policymakers and others are not supported by the overall empirical evidence.'
sources.project_applicability: Primary source and sole mechanism grounding for all 12 LETF_* primary candidates -- the rule's existence (large-move-conditioned rebalancing flow), the reason a long-only reversal rule is the executable subset, and the honest prior (survey itself expects economic insignificance).

The survey synthesizes, but this iteration does not separately open, the underlying papers it reviews (Ivanov & Lenkey, Cheng & Madhavan, a 2022 SFI working paper) -- those remain unverified primary sources, not cited independently here.

existing_solution_comparison: `oc research directions check letf` and `check dip` (run this session) found no prior local test of this specific magnitude-conditioned-reversal mechanism -- the registry's dir:letf_close_rebalancing_flow_reversal entry itself is 'queued' (added by the 2026-09-29 gap search, this task's own source), and the only related prior local iterations are dir:etf_dip_reversion_ibs_connors (a different, RSI(2)/IBS-based dip signal, refuted 2026-09-24 -- companion iteration h20260929_01_dip_rejudge re-judges it) and dir:option_expiration_week_calendar_effect (a different, calendar-anchored dealer-hedging-flow mechanism, refuted 2026-09-29, 0/8 primary, negative anchor Sharpe on all 8). Neither prior iteration tested a same-ticker magnitude-conditioned drop-then-reversal rule; this is the first local test of that specific mechanism. The Lenkey (2024) survey itself is the primary and only genuinely new source opened this round (its own literature review already surveys Ivanov & Lenkey, Cheng & Madhavan, and other prior LETF-flow papers, so a second independent read of those underlying papers was judged low-value given the survey's own synthesis already states the class-level conclusion); the remaining sources below are reused, already-verified local evidence (short-horizon-reversal academic grounding, and this project's own prior refutations of adjacent flow/calendar mechanisms) rather than newly-fetched sources, per the mission's reuse-before-repeat rule.
negative_experiments_checked: h20260928_42_opex_week (another mechanical dealer/hedging-flow mechanism, refuted: 0/8 primary, all negative anchor Sharpe, corroborated by an internal placebo) and h20260924_01_etf_dip_reversion (0/24 at G1/G1', D1's placebo failure) both set the recent-round base rate: published flow/reversal mechanisms have repeatedly failed this project's specific 10bp/20bp next-open-fill K1/K2 contract even where the underlying academic mechanism is judged real. Lenkey (2024)'s own synthesis already reads the LETF-rebalancing-flow literature as 'economically insignificant' despite statistically significant associations in individual papers -- this batch is a direct, cheap test of whether that holds under this project's specific contract, not an assumption that it does.
